summary: REQUEST_CHANGES on PR #399 exact head 2c33c31f3ab96528308f01d18a72d2446adb1553. The new owned-handle wrapper correctly coordinates the copied destroy() function, but table.clone(realized) also republishes the live RealizedLab.model Roblox Model. Callers of start()/get() can still invoke lab.model:Destroy() directly, bypassing owned.destroy(), leaving the underlying runtime/representation teardown uncoordinated and private current non-nil; the next start() remains fenced against a dead physical lab. The current regression proves the raw destroy function was replaced but does not cover direct mutable model authority. Preserve minimum read/diagnostic access without exporting an uncoordinated lifecycle-capable Model reference, or explicitly coordinate out-of-band model destruction back into matching harness/runtime teardown; add a direct-model destruction regression. Canonical CI green is not disputed. No Studio/two-client evidence is claimed.
evidence: PR #399 bindOwnedHandle shallow-clones the full RealizedLab and replaces only owned.destroy; RealizedLab includes model: Model.
PhysicsLabRealizer.destroy() performs model destruction, representation clearing, and runtime disposal, while direct model destruction bypasses those latter ownership teardown steps.
Bootstrap currently uses the returned lab.model only for read-only attribute inspection, so a narrower read/diagnostic surface is feasible without claiming a specific implementation architecture.
GitHub review 4910825181 records the exact-head REQUEST_CHANGES verdict.
